PESTICIDE -- BIFENTHRIN, TECHNICAL -- SPECIFICATION

Pesticides and Pesticides Residues Analysis Sectional Committee, FAD 1

FOREWORD This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Pesticides and Pesticides Residues Analysis Sectional Committee had been approved by the Food and Agriculture Division Council. Bifenthrin is an insecticide, largely used in the preparation of insecticidal formulations. Bifenthrin is the common name accepted by the International Organization for Standardization (ISO) for 2-methylbiphenyl-3-ylmethyl-(1RS,3RS)-3-[(Z)-2-chloro-3,3,3-trifluoroprop-1-enyl]-2,2-dimethylcyclopropanecarboxylate. The empirical formula and structural formula and molecular mass of bifenthrin are given below: Empirical Formula C23H22ClF3O2
F3 C C Cl H CH3 H CH CH3 CO2CH 2

Structural Formula (Z)-(1R)-cisCH3

Molecular Mass 422.9

(Z)-(1S)-cisH Cl C F3C CH CH3 CO2CH2 CH3 H CH3

In the formulation of this standard, due consideration has been given to the provisions of Insecticides Act, 1968 and the Rules framed thereunder. However, this standard is subject to the restrictions imposed under the Insecticides Act, 1968 and Rules, wherever applicable. For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 `Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised)'. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

IS 15936 : 2011

Indian Standard PESTICIDE -- BIFENTHRIN, TECHNICAL -- SPECIFICATION
1 SCOPE This standard prescribes the requirements and the methods of sampling and test for bifenthrin, technical. 2 REFERENCES The following standards contain provisions which through reference in this text, constitute provisions of this standard. At the time of publication, the editions indicated were valid. All standards are subject to revision and parties to agreements based on this standard are encouraged to investigate the possibility of applying the most recent editions of the standards indicated below: IS No. 1070 : 1992 6940 : 1982 8190 (Part 1) : 1988 10946 : 1996 Title Reagent grade water (third revision) Methods of test for pesticides and their formulations ( first revision) Requirements for packing of pesticides: Part 1 Solid pesticides (second revision) Methods of sampling for technical grade pesticides ( first revision) 200 kg MS drums. Closures provided shall be such as not to allow any materials to leak through them. These shall be leak proof and pilfer proof. The packing shall also comply with the general requirements as specified in IS 8190 (Part 1). 5 MARKING 5.1 The container shall be marked legibly and indelibly with the following information and other additional information, as is required under the Insecticides Act, 1968, and Rules framed thereunder: a) b) c) d) e) f) g) h) j) Name of the material; Name and address of the manufacturer; Batch number or Code number; Date of manufacture; Date of expiry; Nominal bifenthrin content, percent (m/m); Net mass of contents; A cautionary notice as worded in Insecticides Act, 1968 and Rules framed thereunder; and Any other information required under Standards of Weights and Measures (Packaged Commodities) Rules, 1977.

3 REQUIREMENTS 3.1 Description The material shall be in the form of off-white to pale tan, crystalline or waxy solid, free from extraneous impurities. 3.2 The material shall comply with the requirements specified in Table 1. 4 PACKING The material shall be packed in clean and dry lacquered

5.2 BIS Certification Marking The product may also be marked with the Standard Mark. 5.2.1 The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The details of the conditions under which the licence for the use of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards.

IS 15936 : 2011 6 SAMPLING Representative samples of the material shall be drawn according to IS 10946. 7 TESTS 7.1 Tests shall be carried out by the methods referred in col 4 and col 5 of Table 1. 7.2 Quality of Reagents Unless specified otherwise, pure chemicals and reagent grade water (see IS 1070) shall be employed in tests.
NOTE -- `Pure chemicals' shall mean chemicals that do not contain impurities which affect the results of test or analysis.

ANNEX A [Table 1, Sl No. (i)]
DETERMINATION OF BIFENTHRIN CONTENT

A-1 GENERAL The bifenthrin content is determined by gas chromatography using internal standard technique. A-2 APPARATUS A-2.1 Gas chromatograph (GLC) equipped with FID with facilities for on column injection and coupled to a printer-plotter- cum -integrator is used for this determination. The suggested operative parameters are as follows, but can be changed, if necessary, provided standardization is done: Column Stainless steel, length = 2 m, OD = 3 mm, packed with 10 percent OV-101 on chromosorb WHP 80/100 mesh a) Column oven -- 250�C b) Detector -- 300�C c) Injector -- 275�C

Carrier gas

a) Nitrogen -- 30 ml/min b) Hydrogen -- 40 ml/min c) Air -- 450 ml/min

Retention time (Guide values)

a) Bifenthrin -- 10.1 min (approximately) b) Docosane -- 5.3 min (approximately)

A typical chromatogram of bifenthrin with internal standard is given in Fig. 1 A-2.2 Injection Volume -- 1 �l. A-2.3 Standard Glassware A-2.4 Microlitre Syringe -- 5/10 �l capacity. A-3 REAGENTS A-3.1 Acetone -- AR grade or equivalent.

IS 15936 : 2011 A.3.2 Internal Standard -- Docosane AR grade or equivalent. A-3.3 Bifenthrin Reference Standard -- Of known purity. A-4 PROCEDURE A-4.1 Preparation of Internal Standard Solution Weigh accurately 1.0 g of docosane into a 100 ml volumetric flask. Dissolve the solids completely in acetone and make up the volume up to the mark with acetone. Shake well to homogenize. A-4.2 Preparation of Analytical Standard Solution Weigh accurately 0.1 g of bifenthrin reference standard of known purity into a 50 ml volumetric flask. Dissolve in 10 ml of acetone. Add 10 ml of the internal standard solution and make up the volume up to the mark with acetone. Shake well to homogenize. A-4.3 Preparation of Sample Solution Weigh accurate quantity of a sample equivalent to about 0.1 g of bifenthrin sample into a 50 ml volumetric flask. Dissolve in 10 ml of acetone. Add 10 ml of the internal standard solution and make up the volume up to the mark with acetone. Shake well to homogenize. A-4.4 Estimation Inject 1 �l standard solution until the internal standard/ reference substance area quotations of two successive chromatograms do not deviate from each other by more than 2 percent. Then use the following injection sequence: . .. . .. ..C S1 S1, C S2 S2, C S3 ............ where C S = standard solution; and = sample solution (1, 2, .. .... n).

From the chromatograms of the standard solution and sample solution, measure the peak areas of the internal standard and bifenthrin peaks, and compute the percentage of the bifenthrin as given in A-5. A-5 CALCULATION Bifenthrin content, percent by mass where M1 = mass of standard bifenthrin in standard solution, in g; M2 = mass of sample taken for test in g; A1 = peak area of bifenthrin in the chromatogram of standard solution; A2 = peak area of bifenthrin in the chromatogram of sample solution; A3 = peak area of internal standard in the chromatogram of standard solution; A4 = peak area of internal standard in the chromatogram of in sample solution; and P = percent purity of bifenthrin reference standard.
NOTES 1 To check on component separation, a sample solution should be run with and without internal standard present. 2 The operating conditions are suggestive and may vary depending on the available GC equipment and ancillary facilities. The actual set of parameters used for the test and standardization should be stated, if different from the above conditions.

ANNEX B [Table 1, Sl No. (ii)]
DETERMINATION OF CIS ISOMER CONTENT IN BIFENTHRIN TECHNICAL B-1 PRINCIPLE The cis isomer content in bifenthrin technical is determined by reverse phase high performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) equipped with UV-VIS detector. B-2 APPARATUS B-2.1 A high performance liquid chromatograph with auto sampler coupled with UV-VIS detector and a printer-plotter- cum -integrator is used for this determination. The suggested operative parameters are 3 as follows, but can be changed, if necessary, provided standardization is done: Column : Stainless steel, 250 mm � 4.6 mm i.d., 5 micron C18 column Detector : UV (230 nm) Temperature : Ambient Solvent system : Acetonitrile : Water (73 : 27 v/v) Solvent flow rate : 1.5 ml/min Sample size : 10 �l Analysis mode : Isocratic

IS 15936 : 2011 A typical HPLC chromatogram of bifenthrin isomers is given in Fig. 2 B-2.2 Microlitre Syringe -- 5/25 �l. B-2.3 Standard Glassware B-3 REAGENTS B-3.1 Acetonitrile -- HPLC grade or equivalent. B-3.2 Water -- HPLC grade or equivalent. B-4 PROCEDURE B-4.1 Preparation of the Sample Solution Weigh accurately 0.1g equivalent of bifenthrin sample into a 50 ml volumetric flask. Prior to weighing, the sample should be allowed to sit at 100�C oven for 15-20 min. Make up the volume upto the mark with acetonitrile. Shake well to homogenize. B-4.2 Estimation Before starting perform two injections of sample solution to equilibrate the system. Carry out duplicate injections of sample solution and record the integrated areas for each peak. B-5 CALCULATION Calculate the average area count for each isomer from the sample injections.

Cis isomer area count in sample � 100 Percent Cis isomer = Cis isomer area + Trans isomer area count in sample
